---
package: "openpipeline"
version: "v4.2.0"
title: "umap"
subtitle: "openpipeline v4.2.0"
toc: true
namespace: "Dimred"
description: "UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) is a manifold learning technique suitable for visualizing high-dimensional data. Besides tending to be faster than tSNE, it optimizes the embedding such that it best reflects the topology of the data, which we represent throughout Scanpy using a neighborhood graph. tSNE, by contrast, optimizes the distribution of nearest-neighbor distances in the embedding such that these best match the distribution of distances in the high-dimensional space. We use the implementation of umap-learn [McInnes18]. For a few comparisons of UMAP with tSNE, see this preprint."
type: "module"
latest: "true"
---

### Arguments

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description

Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--min_dist`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The effective minimum distance between embedded points. Smaller values will result in a more clustered/clumped embedding where nearby points on the manifold are drawn closer together, while larger values will result on a more even dispersal of points. The value should be set relative to the spread value, which determines the scale at which embedded points will be spread out.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `0.5`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--spread`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The effective scale of embedded points. In combination with `min_dist` this determines how clustered/clumped the embedded points are.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `1.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--num_components`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The number of dimensions of the embedding.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `2`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--max_iter`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The number of iterations (epochs) of the optimization. Called `n_epochs` in the original UMAP. Default is set to 500 if neighbors['connectivities'].shape[0] <= 10000, else 200.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alpha`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The initial learning rate for the embedding optimization.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `1.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--gamma`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Weighting applied to negative samples in low dimensional embedding optimization. Values higher than one will result in greater weight being given to negative samples.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Default]{.arg-key} `1.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--negative_sample_rate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The number of negative edge/1-simplex samples to use per positive edge/1-simplex sample in optimizing the low dimensional embedding.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `5`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--init_pos`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
How to initialize the low dimensional embedding. Called `init` in the original UMAP. Options are:

* Any key from `.obsm`
* `'paga'`: positions from `paga()`
* `'spectral'`: use a spectral embedding of the graph
* `'random'`: assign initial embedding positions at random.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"spectral"`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/dimred/umap/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/dimred/umap);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/dimred/umap/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
